title: A Braid of Bright Threads
story:
The rain on the high glass panes grew lighter, then softer, then settled into a slow, rhythmic drip. The clatter of Mateo's loom had quieted too, leaving only the tranquil hush of the Glass Passage. James sat nestled on the low rim of a carved stone planter near the passage's exit, resting the bundle of dyed yarn across his small knees. There were strands the indigo blue of deep mountain shadows. There were strands the saffron yellow of noon sunlight. There were strands the vivid crimson of ripe cliffberries.

Taking the ends of the colored fibers in his nimble fingers, James set to work. With patient, practiced dexterity learned from untangling vines in the Great Canopy, he looped and twisted the threads, braiding them into a sturdy, vibrant cord. He wound the braid snugly around the worn brown leather strap holding Barnaby's brass canister, knotting it securely against the buckle. Where the plain leather had once blended into the wet shadows of rainy alleys, it now carried a bright, defiant splash of color—a tangible piece of the highland city bound to his journey.

When the clouds overhead began to part, bathing the vaulted glass in pale amber light, James stood and tested the strap across his chest. He padded through the tall iron-and-glass archway and stepped out into the Plaza of the Fountain. The air was cool and crisp, smelling of wet limestone and damp earth. Pigeons strutted across the glistening cobblestones, and thin ribbons of rainwater gurgled through carved street gutters toward a wide, tiered stone fountain that dominated the center of the square.

James hopped onto the stone rim of the fountain's lowest pool, peering down into the calm water. He saw the clouds drifting high above Oakhaven, he saw the distant stone dome of the Grand Library reflected upside-down, and he saw himself—small against the sweeping stone town, but steady, grounded, and carrying a new thread of its story.
location: The Plaza of the Fountain, Oakhaven
